criteria.name: Specific customer and specific future state, not a platitude
criteria.rationale: Customer & Problem names "the thirty-two seat neighbourhood room with one prep cook and no analyst" and explicitly excludes chains, with a concrete failure mode ("hotel pans of Sunday's mise... none of it sellable by Wednesday"). Future State names a dated end condition — "In three years, a thirty-two seat independent has the same demand number a fifty-unit chain's analyst produces — day by day, dish by dish, without hiring one" — which is a state of the world, not a "make lives better" platitude.

criteria.name: Commits to a grounding factor (insight / trend / technology bet)
criteria.rationale: Grounding Insight commits to a named technology trend and an explicit bet: POS systems "now push item-level sales through an API — timestamped, going back years" versus the prior "monthly PDF export," and "the bet is that the signal needed to forecast a thirty-two seat room is already sitting in that history, and is recoverable at that scale." It also commits to a falsifiable scope claim — "the product is the number itself, not the prep schedule" — which is a real product bet rather than altitude.

criteria.name: Something a reader could point to and say "this didn't happen"
criteria.rationale: The Vision Pivot Trigger specifies an observable test and an observable negative result: "Put it into ten kitchens and measure prepped-food waste. If that waste doesn't move at all, the premise was wrong." It adds a second distinct disconfirming outcome — waste turning out to live in ordering rather than prep timing — so a reader has concrete conditions to point at. The absence of a numeric threshold or deadline weakens it but does not make it unfalsifiable.

criteria.name: Vision Statement swap-test
criteria.rationale: "The demand number every chain has an analyst for, for the thirty-two seat kitchen that doesn't — read straight out of the POS they already run" carries three specifics that break on swap: the chain-analyst parity claim, the explicitly analyst-less independent as the customer, and the existing-POS mechanism. A chain-focused analytics vendor or a POS incumbent could not say this and have it ring true, since their whole position is the analyst-having customer this statement defines itself against.

criteria.name: Future State swap-test
criteria.rationale: The future state is stated as a specific operator's changed Tuesday — "Renata preps Sunday for what Thursday will actually sell, and the Tuesday walk-in has nothing in it to carry to the bin" — plus "the forecast stops being the thing only the chains can afford." Swapping in a competitor whose customer is the fifty-unit chain inverts the sentence rather than preserving it, so the swap breaks.

criteria.name: Why Us / Why Now extended swap-test
criteria.rationale: The Why Us is not competitor-portable: it rests on "eleven years cooking, two independent kitchens run," chefs taking calls from chefs, and a specific unaskable question — "What did you throw out Tuesday" — that "no operator would ever put on a form for a stranger." The two-years-ago half is the artifact's thinnest point, since the timing clause dates the POS API shift against "a decade ago" rather than establishing recency, but "left six months ago" is a hard recency marker that was not true two years ago, so the field as a whole survives.
